title: RegistryRelease
description: The manifest of one publication of the BACP registry files (the handler registry and the conformance-authority list). It lets a Mandate Manager or a gateway tell which of two copies is newer without trusting a gateway's clock or a copy served by a gateway, and fixes the instant from which the 24-hour freshness rule runs. Every publication, including a backport that amends a dated release in place, raises registry_serial. There is no registry-signed snapshot: no party holds a registry signing key, so the dated release is the only source.

registry_version.description: The dated BACP release (YYYY-MM-DD, for example 2026-10-18) that this publication belongs to.

registry_serial.description: The publication counter. It starts at 1 and strictly increases across every publication of the registry files, across dated releases and across backports to a dated release, so that two publications of the same registry_version are ordered. A replica that holds a lower serial than the one recorded for a pause is stale.

published_at.description: When this publication became available, as an RFC 3339 timestamp in IST (+05:30). The 24-hour freshness clock of a gateway, and of a Mandate Manager, runs from this instant.

uri.description: Where the file is, as a URI reference resolved against the location of this manifest, so that the same manifest is valid in every published version.

digest.description: sha-256 over the RFC 8785 (JCS) form of the parsed JSON file, as 'sha-256:' and the unpadded base64url digest. It is not a hash of the file's bytes, because the site build re-serialises each JSON file.
